# pantechdynamics_webhook (Resource)

A webhook: an https URL Pantech sends your organization's events to, as signed JSON POST requests. Every argument changes in place. The signing secret is shown once, when the webhook is created, and is kept in state as secret. Rotating the secret is done in the console or the CLI, not by Terraform; after a rotation, the secret in state is stale. At most 10 webhooks per organization, and only an API key made by an owner or admin can manage them. Webhooks are free.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Send instance and volume events, and paid invoices, to your own endpoint.
# Every delivery is a JSON POST signed with the webhook's secret.
resource "pantechdynamics_webhook" "ops" {
  url         = "https://hooks.example.com/pantech"
  description = "Production alerts"
  events = [
    "instance.*",           # every instance event
    "volume.attach_failed", # one exact event type
    "invoice.paid",
  ]
}

# Subscribe to everything, but keep it paused for now.
resource "pantechdynamics_webhook" "audit" {
  url     = "https://audit.example.com/pantech"
  events  = ["*"]
  enabled = false
}

# The signing secret is shown only when the webhook is created, so it lives in
# Terraform state. Hand it to the receiver, for example through a secret store.
# Rotating it is done in the console or the CLI, not by Terraform.
output "ops_webhook_secret" {
  value     = pantechdynamics_webhook.ops.secret
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `events` (List of String) What the webhook subscribes to, 1 to 100 entries, each listed once: an event type such as "instance.created" (see the pantechdynamics_webhook_event_types data source), "<resource>.*" for every event of one resource (for example "instance.*"), or "*" for everything. The order is kept.
- `url` (String) Where events are sent: an https URL on the public internet, at most 2,048 characters, with no user name or password.

### Optional

- `description` (String) A note for yourself, at most 255 characters. Defaults to "".
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether events are sent to the webhook. Defaults to true. The platform disables a webhook whose deliveries have failed for three days (disabled_reason = "failing"); the next apply with enabled = true enables it again, which clears its failure history.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the webhook was created, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.
- `disabled_reason` (String) Why the webhook is disabled: "disabled_by_user", or "failing" after three days of failed deliveries. Null while it is enabled.
- `failing_since` (String) When deliveries started failing with no success since, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second. Null while they succeed.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the webhook, starting with whk_.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The signing secret (whsec_...), used to verify the Pantech-Signature header of each delivery. The platform shows it only in the create response, so it exists only in Terraform state: treat the state as a secret. It is null after an import, and it does not follow a rotation made in the console or CLI.
- `updated_at` (String) When the webhook last changed, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A webhook is imported by its id. Its signing secret cannot be read back, so
# secret is null after an import.
terraform import pantechdynamics_webhook.ops whk_06gge7avbst1z09taja09tkkeg
```
